findings.title: Raw recovery codes sent to user storage instead of hashed codes
findings.body: The user-storage path passes the raw generatedCodes JSON as the credential value (`recoveryCodesJson`). The local path stores hashed codes via the credential model. A federated store therefore receives plaintext one-time recovery codes. The test storage provider compares raw input with the raw stored codes. Any real provider that tries to hash them or treat them like local data gets inconsistent semantics. Also the local provider's `createCredential` may apply side effects, such as removing old credentials, that the user-storage path skips.

findings.title: Federated credential lookup breaks consumption tracking
findings.body: `getCredential` returns the federated credential first. But `RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator` then calls `removeStoredCredentialById` on it, which only works for local storage. Used codes are never marked used in user storage. The test provider's `getCredentials` rebuilds the model with `createFromValues` on every call, so `getNextRecoveryAuthnCode` always returns code 0 and the same code is requested forever. Federated recovery codes are effectively reusable, and `allCodesUsed` can never become true.

findings.title: Unchecked Optional.get() calls
findings.body: `credentialModelOpt.get()` and `getNextRecoveryAuthnCode().get()` throw NoSuchElementException when no credential exists or no codes remain. The previous code had the same weakness, but the new lookup adds more paths on which the Optional can be empty.

findings.title: getCredentials NPE and lost user label
findings.body: `getMyUser(user)` can return null, for example for a user that has been removed. `myUser.recoveryCodes` then throws an NPE, unlike the null checks elsewhere in this class. The model built from `createFromValues` also has a random id and never sets the stored credential id. It therefore does not match the `recoveryCodesModel` id created in `updateCredential`.
